newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: MORE POSITIVE REACTION TO CAR INDUSTRY TARIFF PLAN
There has been futher positive reaction to the Federal Government's freeze on car industry tariffs.
Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett has welomed the plan, describing it as sensible and pragmatic.
Tariffs will be cut from 22% to 15% by the year 2000, and will stay at that level for four years.
They will then be reduced to 10 % in the year 2005.

Mr Kennett says the pause in tariff reductions gives the car industry time to better position itself, and removes a very big, black cloud for thousands of people directly and indirectly employed in the automotive industry.
South Australian Premier John Olsen says the tariff decision means car makers, such as Mitsubishi, can forge ahead with the plans for their Adelaide operations.
Meanwhile, South Australia's employers chamber says the decision will provide a much needed confidence boost to the State's economy.
Chief Executive Lindsay Thompson says the improvement of prospects for the car and component industries will flow on to other smaller businesses.
SIR RONALD SAYS DODSON QUALIFIED TO MAKE COMMENTS

President of the Human Rights Commission, Sir Ronald Wilson, says ATSIC Social Justice Commissioner, Mick Dodson, is perfectly qualified to make the comments he made on the Stolen Children report at an conference on child welfare.

Mr Dodson told an international forum Australia was guilty of genocide in its past policy of taking Aboriginal children from their families, and now practises a more covert form of cultural destruction.
Aboriginal Affairs minister, John Herron, said he hated Australians dumping on their country, overseas.
But Sir Ronald has told ABC Radio, Mr Dodson was speaking only in a seminar of the conference, focusing on children.
MOORE SAYS JOBS WILL FLOW FOLLOWING CAR TARIFFS DEAL
Federal Industry Minister John Moore says jobs will flow through as a result of the Government's plan on car industry tariffs.
The Government has decided to freeze car industry tariffs at 15-per cent in the year 2000, before lowering them to 10-per cent in 2005.
Mr Moore says the Government is committed to industry reform, and the tariff freeze will provide certainty and allow investment in Australia's car manufacturing industry to continue.
Mr Moore has told ABC Radio, he expects $4 billion worth of investment will flow into the country's car industry.
He says while Australian manufacturers still have a way to go to get up to world competition, the Government's plan will enable them to do so.
SURGE IN DEMAND FOR EXECUTIVES COULD LEAD TO MORE JOBS
A leading executive search firm says a surge in the demand for business executives could point towards improving general employment trends.
EL Australian Consulting says demand for executives is a leading indicator for pick-ups in broader employment, because managers are usually hired before other workers in business expansion.
The EL Index has climbed 25% in the past quarter, meaning 400 more executive jobs are being advertised around the country now than in February.
EL Consulting Managing Director, Grant Montgomery, says the increase is a clear sign of growing confidence in the economy.
MCGRATH SAYS TUBBY'S FORM IMPORTANT TO SIDE
Australian fast bowler Glen McGrath says the form of Captain Mark Taylor is important to the team, and would boost the side if he scored some runs.
Taylor was bowled out for seven in the first Ashes Test against England at Edgebaston overnight, in Australia's dismal first innings total of 118.
At the end of play yesterday, England reached three for 200.
Glen McGrath has told ABC Radio the team has not yet given up on the first test.
Meanwhile, Victorian pace bowler Paul Reiffel is hoping to receive a call to join Australia, following an injury to Jason Gillespie in the first Ashes cricket Test overnight.
Gillespie has torn a hamstring and is not expected to bowl for the remainder of this test, opening the door for Reiffel.
Reiffel, a shock omission from the original touring party, has kept up his training and says he is ready to go.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
